reasons: The scope of work for an AI-assisted permit intake and completeness automation platform under FR-1 through FR-10 directly matches the firm's core business of building automation platforms and AI-integrated ops software.
The calculated weighted fit score of 7.25 exceeds the minimum threshold of 5, supported by strong delivery capabilities and zero FAIL gates.
The budget ceiling of $420,000 provides an attractive revenue opportunity for a small engineering studio delivering cloud-hosted software over a 3-year contract term.
summary: The City of Port Alder is soliciting proposals for an AI-assisted permit intake and plan review automation platform to reduce application returns and shorten processing time.
The platform must integrate with the City's PermitCore v9 system, perform automated completeness checks across 46 permit types, and assist staff without replacing licensed human reviewers.
Proposals are set aside for Small Businesses (fewer than 100 employees and under $15M average gross receipts) and must be submitted electronically via Port Alder Bids by January 15, 2027.
The contract term is 3 years with two 1-year renewal options, funded under a budget ceiling of $420,000 for implementation and the first two years of service.

evaluation_method.value: Written proposal evaluation (100 points) covering Technical Approach (30), Experience (20), Cost (20), Key Personnel (15), Implementation Plan (10), and Responsible AI/Security (5); followed by finalist virtual demonstrations (up to 25 points), reference checks, and negotiation.

evidence.quote:
The City will award to the Proposer whose proposal offers the best overall value, which may not be the
lowest price. The written score and the demonstration score are added together to rank finalists.

fit_factors.reason: The required scope of designing an AI-assisted permit intake, completeness checking, and workflow routing system integrated via REST/SOAP APIs under requirements FR-1 through FR-10 directly aligns with the company's core focus on building automation platforms and AI-integrated ops software.

Eligibility is scored neutrally at 5 because key prerequisites—including the 3-year business history under MQ-1, past public-sector AI projects under MQ-2, Washington UBI registration under MQ-3, and the small business set-aside limits under Section 10—depend on unconfirmed company facts.

The firm's small senior team is well-suited to build web-based intake portals and AI review tools within the 3-year contract term, provided a designated Project Manager can attend the mandatory in-person kickoff in Port Alder per MQ-4.

Commercial risk is moderate because while the $420,000 budget cap must cover 4 implementation phases plus 2 years of hosting, subscription, and AI model fees, the firm must also absorb strict UAT accuracy thresholds (90% completeness accuracy) and carry $2,000,000 in professional and cyber liability insurance under Section 8.

what_would_change_my_mind: Having less than 3 years of operating history as of January 15, 2027 would trigger a mandatory rejection under Minimum Qualification 1.
Lacking at least two completed public-sector or regulated-industry AI/workflow automation projects in the last 5 years would fail Minimum Qualification 2.
Inability to assign a Project Manager who can attend the project kickoff in person in Port Alder would violate Minimum Qualification 4.
open_questions_for_agency: Can the City clarify if third-party AI model consumption costs (API fees) must be fully wrapped into the $420,000 ceiling, or if high usage volume can be billed separately?
Will the City allow remote participation for the project kickoff if travel conditions restrict the Project Manager's in-person attendance required by Minimum Qualification 4?
What specific test dataset size will DPI use during UAT to measure the 90% completeness agreement and 3% false-complete threshold specified in the performance metrics?
